case_title: MAHADEVAPPA v. STATE OF KARNATAKA REP. BY PUBLIC PROSECUTOR
aggravating_circumstances: Demand of dowry, ill-treatment, assault, addiction to liquor, presence of kerosene oil bottle, burn injuries on upper body
neutral_facts: The accused, a newlywed husband, was addicted to alcohol and frequently demanded money from his wife and her parents. He also subjected his wife to physical abuse and harassment. The wife eventually suffered severe burn injuries and died as a result. The prosecution presented evidence indicating that the accused poured kerosene oil on his wife and set her on fire. The incident occurred in the house where only the accused and the deceased were present. The deceased's body showed signs of burn injuries on the upper part, and kerosene oil was found on her body. A kerosene oil bottle was also found in the room. The deceased's family and relatives testified about the accused's behavior and the circumstances leading to her death. The prosecution argued that the accused's actions were intentional and not accidental.
